author: reek
body: A gauge asked to show more than its maximum, and an input whose caret is sixty characters past a field that holds a couple of dozen. Both must stop at their own right edge.

author: reek
body: Moved from `codex/test/gop-render-clamp` when `apps/guios/GopRender.codex` retired. Same two questions, same two over-range values; what changed is the subject, which is now the compositor that actually ships, and the instrument, which reads the framebuffer with `peek-32` instead of a GopBuf with `gop-buf-get`.

author: reek
body: The instrument has to scan OUTSIDE the widget and that is the whole design. An over-wide fill and a one-pixel caret are written exactly as correct ones are, so a reading that asks only whether either is present answers yes in both worlds. What distinguishes them is where the paint stops, so each arm counts the subject's colour in the band to the RIGHT of its bounds, where nothing should ever appear.

author: reek
body: The buffer is wider than the widget for the same reason: `gop-fill-rect` clips to the buffer, so a buffer the size of the widget would swallow the escape it exists to catch.

author: reek
body: The subject is pinned to 200 wide inside a 400-wide buffer and a flexible label takes the rest, so there is a 200-pixel band to the right of it that belongs to nobody.
